media.caption: Mid-tenth-century ivory icon; the missing wings once formed a triptych. Probable private devotional use is an interpretation. Three modern numbered notes point to surviving features on the unchanged photograph; their observations remain separate from interpretation.

items.label: Openwork above the figures
items.text: Openings pierce the carved frame above the central figure. The museum describes an architectural canopy with columns carved in openwork. This is an ivory representation, not a measured plan of a known building.

items.label: A figure projects from the background
items.text: The central body projects in front of the flatter surface behind it. A carver left material for the figure while removing material around it. The photograph does not establish a specific tool, exact carving depth, maker or workshop.

items.label: Letters beside a debated figure
items.text: Greek-letter lines appear near the reclining lower figure. Frazer compared the abbreviated inscription, other images and hymns to argue for Hades rather than Adam. Identifying the figure requires that cited interpretation; it is not an unassisted translation from this photograph.
